newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA COMPLETES AUTUMN SOWING, 1.5 MLN HA SOWN.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA COMPLETES AUTUMN SOWING, 1.5 MLN HA SOWN.

text.p: Bulgaria has completed its autumn sowing and has sown 1.5 mln hectares with wheat and barley, nearly meeting its target of 1.6 million hectares of grain, an agriculture ministry official said on Wednesday.

"We consider this year's sowing successful as wheat sowings have covered some 1.2 million hectares, while some 280,000 hectares have been sown with barley," ministry spokeswoman Roza Trichkova told Reuters.
In 1995 Bulgaria sowed one million ha with wheat and 270,000 ha with barley.
Trichkova said Bulgaria will not face bread shortages next year as enough wheat for human consumption has been sown.
"1996 will be the last year with a grain problem for the country," she said.
Debt-ridden Bulgaria initially delayed its autumn sowing of wheat and barley due to lack of funds and incentives to farmers and because of record high interest rates for loans.
In a bid to speed up the sowing and stave off further shortages, the parliament passed a law in October unblocking farmers' funds from banks placed in receivership by the central bank.
Under the bill, the domestic purchase prices of wheat, maize and barley from the 1996/97 harvest will be no less than 80 percent of the international price.
Trichkova said those measures, plus favourable weather conditions which prolonged the planting period, boosted the autumn sowing.
Last year low domestic prices encouraged high exports, which combined with a poor harvest last summer to produce an acute grain shortage.
